Mark Clancy, whose performances in the winter won him the title of Belgrave's most improved youth. - Photo: Ron Linstead

The big day our lads had spent months building up for saw us finish a dissappointing eighth. Once again only Mark Clancy (153rd) ran to form. Bill Curtin (28th) led the team home with Peter Carton four places behind.
Back on the track, there signs of life returning to Track Captain Adrian Major, while in the 1,500m. Jim Rimmer and young Mark Clancy caught the eye.
It was good to see Paddy Breslin back in action in the junior events, and to see John Stow back in winning form, while there was a promising junior steeplechase from Mark Clancy.
Mark Clancy maintained his recent improvement to finish 5th and in 8th place was Pat Breslin free for once from the heartbreaking series of injuries which have made his winter season so miserable.
Tony Binda was second, half a minute in arrears, and third was John Stow. Mark Clancy filled fourth spot with injury plagued Pat Breslin in fifth position.
Mark Clancy was 60th out of 160 odd finishers and he was probably the only Belgrave runner of the day senior junior or youth to really rise to the big occasion and pull out a best ever effort.
We are becoming accustomed to these sorts of performances by this quartet. A word, however, of commendation for Mark Clancy, who gave admirable backing with his 47th position.

In the junior race, our famous four were 11th, with Peter Carton, who just missed a junior international,vest getting good support for his 10th place from Tony Binda (58th), Bill Curtin (109th) and John Stow (111th), and Mark Clancy again poised to fill any breach that should appear.

TONY BINDA, Peter Carton and Bill Curtin yet again filled the first three places in the final Surrey League. With Mark Clancy (5th) and Paddy Breslin (7th) Belgrave were runaway winners of both match and League title.
